summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: one botanical-biotin RCT and one post-sleeve-gastrectomy observational study. Biotin nutrition credit stays on its separate pathway, and the existing laboratory-test interference warnings (safety owner) are unaffected; no beauty credit. Neither source supports credit for generic biotin. The only RCT (40896024) tested a botanical Sesbania extract (Orgen-Bio, 2.5 mg biotin/day) with mostly within-group, implausibly large effects and a maker-employed author, and the returned A046 decision rejects essentiality-to-beauty inference; 32762597 is uncontrolled observational data showing low efficacy (P=.2). The record becomes reference-only, which removes biotin Evidence points from dependent products (about 123 per the closure plan).

identity.standardization: Sesbania grandiflora extract standardized for 0.5% biotin; 250 mg extract equivalent to 1.25 mg biotin per capsule. Not isolated d-biotin.

population.description: 105 healthy adults aged 20-60 (non-pregnant, non-lactating) with complaints of hair fall, thin, dry and brittle hair and dry skin, randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, Orgen-Bio, or Orgen-Bio plus bamboo silica; 97 completed 90 days. Baseline biotin status was not measured.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized (1:1:1, block), double-blind, placebo (maltodextrin)-controlled, single-center 90-day trial at a contract research site (NovoBliss, Ahmedabad); completers-only analysis; within-group paired tests and between-group t/Mann-Whitney tests.

outcomes.name: Primary hair fall (60-second combing), Orgen-Bio arm: 20.61 +/- 14.39 at day 90 (36.19% reduction from baseline, p<0.001); reported as a '162.24%' reduction versus placebo (p<0.001). Primary endpoints also included hair thickness, density, growth rate and PGA brittle-nail score, largely reported as within-group change.
Secondary skin hydration, elasticity, wrinkles, texture and hair strength: reported within-group improvements; placebo hair-strength proportion also rose (63.64% to 96.97%).

limitations: 21.75 mg silica versus 10 mg Si is a substance-basis distinction, not necessarily a contradictory silica amount.
Botanical biotin and mixture findings do not establish essentiality-based cosmetic benefit for all biotin products.
Returned decision: Source-content hold; reject essentiality-to-beauty-benefit inference.

No credit: the intervention is a whole Sesbania grandiflora extract (0.5% biotin), not the isolated biotin this generic record represents, and the returned A046 decision rejects inferring cosmetic benefit from biotin's essentiality.

Low internal credibility: single-center contract-research study, completers-only analysis, many endpoints reported mostly as within-group change, implausible magnitudes (for example a '162.24%' reduction versus placebo), and an author employed by the ingredient maker (Orgenetics).
Participants were not shown to be biotin deficient; the trial does not establish benefit of biotin supplementation for hair, skin or nails in general.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

dose.administration_frequency: One capsule two times a day after each meal (Table 'Mode of Usage').
co_therapies: Medicated/prescription and anti-thinning hair products (e.g., minoxidil) discontinued; participants used only the study treatments. Silica (Bambusa arundinacea, 21.75 mg silica = 10 mg Si per capsule) present only in the separate combination arm.
dose.reported_regimen: Orgen-Bio capsule: 250 mg Sesbania grandiflora extract equivalent to 1.25 mg biotin, one capsule two times daily after meals, 90 days.

normalization.basis: 1.25 mg biotin per capsule x 2 capsules/day (Mode of Usage row applies to all test treatments) = 2.5 mg/day; the abstract's '1.25 mg' is the per-capsule amount.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC12397994): Methods study design paragraph, Table 2 (test treatments, dosage form, mode of usage, manufacturer), inclusion criteria, statistics; Results primary endpoints; conflicts of interest.

identity.preparation: Biotin 1000 mcg/day (product and form not reported in the abstract).

population.description: 156 women followed 1 year after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy; 112 (72%) had hair loss; 22 biotin-deficient patients were prescribed biotin and 29 took biotin on their own initiative despite optimal levels.

study_contexts.study_design: Single-center observational cohort with non-randomized biotin use; no placebo or randomized control.

dose.administration_frequency: 1000 mcg/day; 3 months for prescribed deficient patients, average 2.5 months for self-initiated users.
dosage_forms: oral biotin supplement (physical form not reported in the abstract)
co_therapies: Postoperative vitamin-deficiency screening and care after sleeve gastrectomy; other supplements not reported in the abstract.
dose.reported_regimen: Biotin 1000 mcg/day for 3 months (prescribed) or about 2.5 months (self-initiated).

normalization.basis: 1000 mcg = 1 mg/day as stated in the abstract.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract (Methods, Results); full text not open access.

outcomes.name: Self-reported remarkable decline in hair loss: 5/22 (23%) biotin-deficient prescribed users and 11/29 (38%) non-deficient self-users; no significant difference between groups (P=.2). Authors conclude biotin showed low efficacy.

limitations: Non-randomized, uncontrolled observational data with subjective hair-loss reporting; cannot carry efficacy credit.
Abstract only; dosage form and product not reported and not inferred.
